figures.finding: English-language screenwriting in Canada is covered by the WGC/CMPA Independent Production Agreement, running 22 May 2024 to 31 January 2027.
figures.applies: Freelance writers of theatrical films, television and other production for CMPA-member and signatory producers.

sources.said: The WRITERS GUILD OF CANADA (the “Guild” or the “WGC”) and The CANADIAN MEDIA PRODUCERS ASSOCIATION (the “Association” or the “CMPA”) May 22, 2024 to January 31, 2027
These agreements set out the terms and conditions for work in all English-language production in Canada

figures.finding: From 1 February 2026 a Canadian feature script pays at least C$71,202; an original treatment C$32,003, a first draft from a treatment C$24,919, a second draft C$21,360 and a polish C$10,664.
figures.applies: Live-action features under the IPA 2024-2027; budgets of C$82,000 or less are negotiable.

sources.said: 3.5% increase to Script Fees as of February 1, 2026 … C101 Script $62,998 $66,148 $68,794 $71,202 C102 Original Treatment $28,316 $29,732 $30,921 $32,003 … C105 First Draft from existing Treatment $22,048 $23,150 $24,076 $24,919 C106 Second Draft from existing First Draft $18,899 $19,844 $20,638 $21,360 … C109 Polish $9,435 $9,907 $10,303 $10,664

figures.finding: A one-hour Canadian TV script pays at least C$21,088 and a half-hour C$10,546 from 1 February 2026; a TV movie script C$53,682.
figures.applies: Television other than movies and mini-series (C402) and TV movies (C301) under the IPA.

figures.finding: On the first day of photography the credited writer is owed a production fee set by budget (for C$2-10m: C$55,825 plus 2.2% of budget above C$2m, times 103%), less script fees paid; above C$13m it is negotiable with a floor of C$300,579.75.
figures.applies: Credited writers under the IPA, paid on the first day of principal photography.

sources.said: On the first day of principal photography, the Producer shall pay each credited Writer … $2,000,000 – $10,000,000 ($55,825 plus 2.2% of the Budget in excess of $2,000,000) x 103% … For a Budget in excess of $13 million the Production Fee is negotiable, but the floor for such negotiation is $300,579.75.

figures.finding: Features under C$3m may pay 40% or 50% of the script fee in four stages, with the balance at photography; under C$1.2m fees may be deferred except C$5,000 on the first day of photography.
figures.applies: IPA Articles C2 (optional incentive plan) and C204.

sources.said: i) forty per cent (40%) of the Script Fee in C101, allocated and paid as follows: a) on signing of the contract 20% b) on delivery of the Treatment 30% c) on delivery of the First Draft Script 25% d) on delivery of the Second Draft Script 25% … five thousand dollars ($5,000) is payable against deferrals on the first day of principal photography

figures.finding: A writing contract covers at most three stages and a polish, and the producer has 30 days after each treatment, outline or first draft to say whether to go on, or is deemed to accept.
figures.applies: All program types under the IPA (Article B1).

sources.said: A contract between a Writer and a Producer shall not provide for more than three stages and a Polish … The Producer shall notify the Writer in writing within thirty (30) calendar days

figures.finding: An option may run at most five years, each year costing at least 10% (5% for features) of the exercise price, which must be at least the minimum script fee; options of three months or less (six for features) are free to negotiate.

value.exercise_min: minimum Script Fee at that stage

sources.said: The Option period, including renewals, which shall not exceed five (5) years; iii) The fee for each year of the Option, which shall not be less than ten percent (10%) per year (five percent (5%) per year in the case of Feature … The fee payable on exercise of the Option, which shall not be less than the minimum Script Fee for such material at the applicable stage of development

figures.finding: The Writers Guild of Canada admits a writer with one signatory contract from the past two years, for a C$350 initiation fee and C$175 annual dues; 2% of fees goes to working dues.

value.eligibility: one writing contract with a signatory producer signed in the past two years

sources.said: you must have one writing contract in our jurisdiction, which has been signed in the past two years with a producer who is “signatory”** … Initiation fee: $350 CAD + Annual dues: $175 CAD = TOTAL: $525 CAD
writers pay 2% of gross fees for member working dues to the WGC

figures.finding: French-language feature writing in Quebec is under the SARTEC/AQPM cinema agreement of 2016-2020, prolonged from 28 November 2021, whose feature script minimum rose to C$50,535; the production fee is 4% of the first C$5m of the budget.
figures.applies: French-language features produced by AQPM members in Quebec.

sources.said: est prolongée pour un an a compter du 28 novembre 2021. … 28-11-2021 au 27-11-2022 (+3%) : 50 535 $

figures.finding: Under the SARTEC/AQPM cinema agreement an option lasts at most one year, each renewal at most six months, at a negotiated price; a first-year option of C$250 or more is deductible from the writing fee.

sources.said: le contrat d'option ne peut excéder une durée d'un (1) an. De plus, chaque renouvellement consécutif est d'une durée d'au plus six (6) mois. … option à condition qu’elle soit égale ou supérieure à 250$;

figures.finding: Canadian feature production in 2024/25 was C$320 million in English and C$140 million in French.

sources.said: French-language production increased by 35% to $140 million, while English-language production decreased by 13.8% to $320 million.

figures.finding: Ontario-based producers made 52% of Canadian feature volume in 2024/25 (C$238m), then Quebec (C$172m).
figures.applies: Canadian theatrical feature film production by producer province.

sources.said: Ontario-based producers accounted for the largest share (52%) of film production in 2024/25, with $238 million in production volume, followed by Quebec ($172 million)
